quote: In this work, we study multi-turn response generation and target on a model that has a simple structure yet can make use of conversation contexts as well as the existing deep models.

We test the proposed approach with three benchmarks including the Ubuntu Dialogue Corpus, DailyDialog, and PERSONA-CHAT... Evaluation results on all three datasets indicate that our model can significantly outperform state-of-the-art generation models in terms of both automatic evaluation and human judgment.
As an important topic in conversational AI, open-domain human-machine conversation is gaining increasing attention from both academia and industry.

quote: We evaluate the performance of the models in terms of response quality with both automatic metrics and human judgment. In automatic evaluation, besides BLEU-4 and perplexity, we follow (Serban et al., 2017) and employ Embedding Average (Average), Embedding Extrema (Extrema), and Embedding Greedy (Greedy) as metrics. We also follow and measure the informativeness of responses with distinct-1 and distinct-2.

In human evaluation, we randomly sample 500 dialogues from each of the three test sets, and recruit 3 native speakers as human annotators. For each context in the 500 dialogues, each annotator compares a response from our model and a response from a baseline model. ... The annotators judge which response is better based on informativeness, consistency, and fluency of the responses.
